messages.author: 3a1d24409cb1ebcd
messages.subject: Vectorization in sampling statement
parts:
Hi all,

So I have a model that compiled and ran without issues, but that didn't use any form of vectorization, so I thought I'd try to speed it up using the new vectorization options (following section 18 of the doc).

Now the relevant part of the model:

---------------------------------
data{
   real<lower=0> mu0;
   real<lower=0> sig0;
}

parameters{
   matrix<lower=0>[K,N] mu;
}

model{
   mu ~ normal(mu0, sig0);
}
--------------------------------

which gives me the following error:

DIAGNOSTICS FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name "normal_log"
   arg 0 type = matrix
   arg 1 type = real
   arg 2 type = real
unknown distribution=normal


I also tried to make mu0 and sig0 matrices, which led to the following error:

DIAGNOSTICS FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name "normal_log"
   arg 0 type = matrix
   arg 1 type = matrix
   arg 2 type = matrix
unknown distribution=normal

--------------------------------

I use version 1.2 of rstan, and ran the model through R. 

Any idea what might be wrong? I can post the entire .stan file if necessary. Any help is appreciated!

Thanks

messages.author: 9d7e54e3329f305f
messages.subject: Re: Vectorization in sampling statement
parts:
Hi Guillaume,

I believe that normal() can return vectors but not matrices. So if you loop through rows of your matrix and vectorize each that will work. e.g.

data {
    int K;
    int N;

real<lower=0> mu0;
    real<lower=0> sig0;
}
parameters {
    matrix<lower=0>[K,N] mu;
}
model {

for (k in 1:K)
        mu[k] ~ normal(mu0, sig0);
}

Best
Kyle

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Vectorization in sampling statement
parts:
On Wednesday, April 10, 2013 7:49:46 PM UTC-4, Kyle Foreman wrote:
model {
    for (k in 1:K)
        mu[k] ~ normal(mu0, sig0);
}
That should be

model {
  for (k in 1:K)

row(mu,k) ~ normal(mu0, sig0);
}

mu[k] would be the element in the k-th row and first column.

Ben

Thanks Kyle, and Ben for your replies. That did solve my problem.

I realized that the documentation didn't mention vectorizing over matrices, so that's my bad. However, this post mentions vectorizing of matrices, so I was a little confused.
Also, assuming that mu0 is a now a matrix of the same dimension as mu, is that legal to write:

model {
  for (k in 1:K)

row(mu,k) ~ normal(row(mu0,k), sig0);
}

Thanks!

In section 20.5 of the manual it states that

Accessing Matrix Rows
If Sigma is a variable of type matrix, then Sigma[1] denotes the first row of Sigma and has the type row_vector. 

so wouldn't mu[k] then be the k-th row of matrix mu (i.e. a row vector, not an element)?

On Wednesday, April 10, 2013 9:08:51 PM UTC-4, Kyle Foreman wrote:
In section 20.5 of the manual it states that

Accessing Matrix Rows
If Sigma is a variable of type matrix, then Sigma[1] denotes the first row of Sigma and has the type row_vector. 

so wouldn't mu[k] then be the k-th row of matrix mu (i.e. a row vector, not an element)?

You're right; it would work either way. Having just been confused by this (for about the millionth time), I think it would be better to write row(mu, k) because it is unambiguous what that is, whereas mu[k] in Stan code generates C++ code that is different from what mu[k] would be in C++ code.

Ben
